title: Unit – 5 : Session – 3 : SLO – 1  |  Graph Traversal — Depth First Search (DFS)
sections: I. Fill in the Blanks
DFS stands for DEPTH FIRST SEARCH.
DFS uses STACK data structure for its implementation.
In DFS, a vertex is marked as VISITED when it has been visited.
The time complexity of DFS for a graph with V vertices and E edges is O(V + E).
DFS traversal can be implemented using both RECURSIVE and ITERATIVE methods.
II. True or False
DFS always visits the shallowest unvisited node first — FALSE (that is BFS).
DFS can be used to detect cycles in a graph — TRUE.
DFS is suitable for finding the shortest path in an unweighted graph — FALSE (BFS is).
The recursive implementation of DFS uses system call stack — TRUE.
III. Short Answer Questions
DFS: a traversal that starts at a vertex and explores as deep as possible along each branch before
backtracking, using a stack (or recursion).
Applications: cycle detection; topological sorting; also maze solving and finding connected components.
Data structure: STACK (explicit or the system call stack in recursion).
DFS vs BFS: DFS explores depth-first using a stack; BFS explores level-by-level using a queue and finds
the shortest path in unweighted graphs.
IV. Solve and Write — Given Undirected Graph (A-H)
Adjacency list:
A -> B, C    B -> A, D, E    C -> A, F, G    D -> B, H
E -> B, H    F -> C, H       G -> C, H       H -> D, E, F, G
DFS traversal from A (neighbours in alphabetical order): A, B, D, H, E, F, C, G
In recursive DFS, the system internally uses the CALL STACK (system stack).
